title: Citizen Science and Amateur Astronomy
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of each line to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line.
passage:
Long before professional observatories dominated the field, (1)___ astronomers were already responsible for a surprising number of significant discoveries, and the tradition has never entirely died out. Today, thanks to affordable telescopes and online (2)___ platforms, this grassroots movement is thriving.

Volunteers now routinely comb through images for supernovae, classify distant galaxies by shape, and flag (3)___ patterns in starlight that might indicate an undiscovered planet. Professional astronomers, whose time is too (4)___ to examine every image individually, increasingly depend on this volunteer workforce to sift through overwhelming quantities of data.

One amateur in the Netherlands became something of a minor celebrity after her (5)___ discovery of a previously unknown exoplanet candidate made international headlines. Sceptics initially worried that crowdsourced data would prove unreliable, riddled with (6)___ identifications made by well-meaning but untrained eyes.

Several peer-reviewed papers have since (7)___ volunteer contributions in their acknowledgements, a level of formal recognition that would have seemed unthinkable a generation ago. For an increasing number of participants, the appeal lies not in fame but in the simple (8)___ of contributing to real scientific research from their own backyard.

questions.explanation: The adjective 'dedicated' (= committed to something) fits before 'astronomers', describing people devoted to the pursuit without being professionals.
The noun 'collaboration' is used attributively before 'platforms' to describe tools designed for people to work together online.
The negative prefix 'un-' gives 'unusual', fitting patterns in starlight that stand out as different from the norm and might signal a planet.
The adjective 'limited' fits after 'too', describing astronomers' time as insufficient for examining every image personally.
The adjective 'accidental' (= happening by chance) fits before 'discovery', describing a find that was not deliberately sought.
The adjective 'erroneous' (= incorrect) fits 'riddled with ___ identifications', describing mistaken classifications made by untrained volunteers.
The verb 'acknowledged', in its past tense form, fits after 'have since', describing papers formally recognising volunteer contributions.
The noun 'satisfaction' fits after 'simple', describing the rewarding feeling of contributing to research rather than seeking fame.
